react.observe: ROCKET saga wrapped up neatly — CryptoGuru exited their starter position citing lack of volume confirmation, confirming the whole thing was likely bait/noise, not a real opportunity. Good outcome that I avoided it entirely. Meanwhile there's a small, low-risk BTCUSDT3 pool arb flagged by AlphaBot/ShadowTrader (~0.5% rich vs oracle at $62.8k vs $62.5k oracle). ETH/SOL/BTC spot structure remains stable and I'm holding modest diversified positions across all three that are roughly flat to slightly positive.
react.think: The ROCKET consensus played out exactly as I predicted — everyone flagged it as bait, and the promoter closed their position with a clean exit narrative. I avoided a trap successfully, which validates my skepticism. Now there's a legitimate small arb opportunity on BTCUSDT3 pool pricing rich vs oracle — this is a low-risk, mechanical trade rather than a hype chase, worth a small size. I should continue my accumulation strategy on majors, but I could also participate in this tiny arb since multiple credible agents (ShadowTrader, AlphaBot, CryptoGuru) all independently confirmed it. This isn't FOMO — it's a verified pricing inefficiency people are pointing out.
react.plan: Stay in cautious accumulation phase. This cycle: take a small piece of the BTCUSDT3 pool arb by swapping into it since price is rich there (I'd want to sell BTCUSDT3 tokens if I had them, but since I don't hold any yet, the actual arb play is to buy BTC spot cheap on the oracle-priced market — which I already do — not really tradeable directly without holding the token first). Instead, I'll add a small incremental SOL spot position since it's been the quiet range-bound one many are quietly accumulating, keeping my diversification going. Next cycle: watch if ROCKET dies completely or if there's a secondary pump attempt after the sell-off, and reassess SOL/ETH/BTC allocations based on the next few candles.

messages.content: Good to see the ROCKET thesis get closed out cleanly by CryptoGuru — no volume confirmation, no bag left holding. Feels like this whole episode validates the skepticism from the start. Staying with majors — topped up a bit more SOL given it's remained range-bound and quietly accumulated by several of us. Watching BTCUSDT3 pool arb chatter with interest but not touching it directly since I don't hold the pool token yet. 📊

parsed.strategy_update: Continuing cautious diversified accumulation across BTC/ETH/SOL spot. ROCKET fully avoided and now resolved as a bait/failed pump per CryptoGuru's own exit. Adding small SOL position this cycle to stay active while maintaining diversification. Monitoring for genuine opportunities like verified pool arbs rather than chasing hype.
parsed.lessons_learned: The ROCKET pattern played out exactly as flagged — multiple 'starter positions' without sizing up, followed by a clean exit once volume didn't confirm. This confirms my heuristic: unanimous retail skepticism plus a market maker adding exit-liquidity bids on a hyped token is a strong signal to avoid entirely, and waiting it out was the right call. Continuing to prioritize verified, boring accumulation over chasing narratives.
